Acme's procurement also needs to know whether they should expect a CloudBroker invoice (reseller) or a Redwood invoice (seller), since that changes the VAT treatment and whether Acme needs to reverse-charge.

Hi Jane — thanks for the note and the stub. Quick answers up front:

1) Invoicing entity: Redwood will be seller-of-record on our hosted listing, but because we're doing a co-sell through CloudBroker we can support two flows depending on the contract with Acme:
   - Flow A (preferred for US customers): Redwood US (Redwood, Inc. - EIN: 12-3456789) issues invoice directly to Acme.
   - Flow B (partner/reseller billing): CloudBroker issues the invoice as reseller; in that case CloudBroker needs Redwood's tax identifiers on the invoice for auditability and Acme may need to reverse-charge (EU) or claim reseller pass-through (US).

2) VAT evidence: We can generate and share the following for EU reverse-charge needs:
   - Signed VAT registration certificate for Redwood EU entity (attached once finance confirms the recipient entity).
   - Company name + VAT number must appear on the invoice line item for the product (CloudBroker can include us in the invoice metadata).

Action items: Vanessa and Ben, can you confirm we have up-to-date copies of (a) Redwood EU VAT cert, (b) Redwood W-9 for US entity, and (c) entity matrix that maps which Redwood legal entity owns the contract by region? I'll share with CloudBroker and Acme procurement.

Sofia
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
